records.name: SHARP Dance Company
records.summary: A modern dance company in Philadelphia that tells stories through movement. Students can take its dance classes or its summer dance intensive, and anyone can see its shows.
records.what_you_do: Take a dance class or sign up for the summer dance intensive, or buy a ticket to a show. Company auditions held in the spring are closed for now.

schedule.text: Dance classes are listed on the site, but no class times are shown. The 2026 summer intensive is open for registration with no dates shown. Upcoming performances include a Richmond, Virginia show on Oct 14, 2026 and a FringeArts run in Philadelphia on Nov 13 and 14, 2026 at 7:30 pm.

locations.label: Company address on its site (a residential building; street not published here)

cost.text: Class and intensive prices are not shown on the site. Show tickets are sold separately.

first_step.how: Call or email the company to ask when the next dance class starts or how to register for the summer intensive, then sign up through the site.
first_step.basis: Classes are listed and the company is open to the public, but the site gives no schedule, prices or beginner information, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The batch id and the Cultural Fund list say 'SHARP Dance Company Copy'. The group's own site and EIN match 'SHARP Dance Company', and no other record for this group exists in data/groups, so this is treated as the group itself, not a duplicate. The id's '-copy' suffix looks like a list error and could be renamed on import. The site gives a residential condo unit as its address, so the street is left out here; the owner should decide whether to publish it. Class times and intensive dates are not on the site.

records.name: Simpatico Theatre
records.notes: A professional theatre company. Its site lists no class, workshop, volunteer, membership or community program. The Community page is a partner list. Jouska PlayWorks is a group of playwrights whose five readings ran in Aug 2024 on a pay what you decide basis, the newest dated item found, and it is recorded as a lead. The Play On! banner points to another theatre's page. The Company page returned 404. The Give and Anti-Racism pages were not read. Not_a_group under the cultural fund rule; re-check if a public class, volunteer or membership role appears.

records.name: South Asian American Digital Archive
records.notes: The group's website returned HTTP 403 on our request, so it was not read and was not retried. No summary, activities, schedule or ways to take part are recorded yet, because nothing could be verified. Needs a manual check of the site before any public text is written.

records.name: Tempesta di Mare
records.summary: Philadelphia's Baroque orchestra. Its musicians play without a conductor and bring back older music in a concert series. Volunteers can usher at concerts, and adults under 40 can join its Young Friends group.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a concert usher by email, or join the Young Friends for discounted season passes and extra events before or after some concerts, such as meeting the musicians. Anyone can buy a ticket to a concert.

schedule.text: Concerts in the 2026 to 27 season include a harpsichord recital on Oct 30 to Nov 1, a violin recital on Nov 12 to 15, and 'A German Advent' on Dec 18 to 20, 2026. Usher dates are set per concert and are not listed.

cost.text: Concert tickets and season passes cost money. Young Friends get 40 percent off subscription packages; for example, a full season pass is $225 for Young Friends instead of $375. No cost is listed for usher volunteers.

first_step.how: Email the group to ask about usher volunteering for the next concert, or buy a Young Friends season pass on the ticketing site and use the Young Friends discount at checkout.
first_step.basis: Ushers are recruited by email and the Young Friends program has a clear online sign-up, but the site does not describe an orientation.

records.notes: The site lists no venue or office address, so no address is recorded. The batch's IRS address is not used. No vocabulary tag fits a Baroque orchestra, so interests are empty and the description is in the summary. A Baroque Music 101 program is linked but no details were found. The under-40 limit applies to Young Friends, not to concerts or ushering.

records.name: The Best Day of My Life So Far
records.summary: A nonprofit that uses storytelling to fight loneliness, mostly among older adults. Partner sites run storytelling groups that bring older adults and younger volunteers together, and the group trains youth and professionals in the same approach.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the sign-up form on its Get Involved page, or ask an organization that serves older adults near you whether it runs a storytelling group. Students can take part in its four-week Grand Camp youth program, which the site describes without dates.

schedule.text: Storytelling groups run in 8-week modules at partner sites, and the site lists no set meeting days or times. Story Pop-Up Events are planned for each location, and none are listed with dates. The Grand Camp program runs four weeks, with no dates listed.

cost.text: Taking part in a storytelling group is free for participants. Partner organizations pay a yearly fee to run the program.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the Get Involved page, and ask an organization that serves older adults near you whether it runs a storytelling group.
first_step.basis: People join through a partner organization or the volunteer form, and the site does not say how to join a group directly.

records.notes: The Updates page has one dated item, 'Looking Ahead Together', dated June 2026 with no day and no link to a post. The newest outside item is a 2024 press feature. A guessed Get Involved path returned 404; the working path is /getinvolved. The site notes that its newsletter sign-up may not be working yet. Its social media posts have no dates in the text read, so they were not used as evidence.

records.name: The Big Picture Alliance
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches digital filmmaking and video skills to young people. Students make their own films, and most programs include a stipend.
records.what_you_do: Apply to one of its youth media programs: a summer teen program, a 9-month teen fellowship, a paid fellowship for young adults, a summer intensive for young adults, or a film studies class for young adults. Most programs require Philadelphia residency.

schedule.text: Fall programs run Sept 15, 2026 to May 25, 2027. The teen fellowship meets Tuesdays 4 to 6 pm, the young adult fellowship Tuesdays 10 am to 3 pm, Media Futures Thursdays 9 am to 3 pm, and the film studies class Wednesdays 4 to 6 pm. Summer intensives run in June and July. Application windows are April 1 to 15 for summer and July 15 to 31 for fall.

cost.text: Free for most programs, and most include a stipend for participation. The cost of the film studies class is not stated.

first_step.how: Watch the programs page for the next application window (April 1 to 15 for summer, July 15 to 31 for fall), then email the address on the page to ask for an application.
first_step.basis: Each program needs an application in a set window and has age and residency limits, so there is no drop-in path.

records.notes: The July application window's year is inferred from the 2026 to 27 program dates on the programs page. The Media Futures listing gives ages 14 to 18 in its eligibility line but 18 to 24 in its description, so confirm with the group. The homepage's newest dated item is a 2024 impact summary, so the 2026 evidence rests on the programs page. Some programs list no street address, so the office is used as the location.

records.name: The Plastic Club
records.summary: A volunteer-run art club in Center City that has supported artists since 1897. It runs weekly drawing and open studio sessions, monthly art shows, and film, music and poetry nights.
records.what_you_do: Drop in to a weekly drawing or open studio session for a small fee, or apply to join the club as a member. Artists can also enter its monthly exhibitions.

schedule.text: Sessions run Monday to Saturday, from mornings into evenings. Examples: Tuesday 9:30 am to 12:30 pm (clothed portrait model), Thursday 5:30 to 8:30 pm (life model), and Saturday 9:30 am to 12:30 pm (croquis with life model). A printmaking open studio runs Saturday 10 am to 2 pm. A Tuesday night Zoom share is also listed.

cost.text: Life model and costume sessions are $10 each ($9 for members, $7 for students). Still life open studio is $5. Printmaking open studio is $10. The membership cost is not listed.

first_step.how: Read the workshop etiquette guide on the club's site, then come to a Thursday or Saturday open studio. New printmaking participants should contact the club's monitor before they come.
first_step.basis: Drawing sessions need no reservation and the club welcomes all artists and interested people, but no beginner class is listed.

records.notes: The batch alias 'The Plastic Club Art Club for Women' is an older name. The current site welcomes all artists, so no community restriction is recorded. The site shows no dated events, so the status is probably_active on the strength of its weekly schedule. Exhibition, open call and membership pages were not read.

records.name: The Primavera Fund
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that mentors young musicians toward top music schools and careers, and helps students with the cost of study. It runs free career sessions for young musicians and keeps an instrument library.
records.what_you_do: Attend one of its free virtual career sessions for young musicians, or ask about its artist mentoring program. The site has a page explaining what a Primavera Artist is, but its application steps were not readable.

schedule.text: Free virtual career sessions were listed for March 11, 18 and 25. The page gives no year and no session times.

locations.label: Mailing address (P.O. Box); sessions are virtual

first_step.how: Watch the homepage for the link to the next free virtual career session, or email the group to ask how to apply to the mentoring program.
first_step.basis: The career sessions are free and open to young musicians, with a link posted for each one. The mentoring application steps are not shown.

records.notes: The session dates have no year on the page, so no dated evidence is recorded and the status rests on a working site. The legal type (grantmaker or public charity) is not stated. The group describes mentoring and financial support programs, so it is listed as a program nonprofit, not a private foundation. The batch's IRS address is not used because the site gives a P.O. box. The Primavera Artist page should be checked by hand.

records.name: The Print Center
records.summary: A free museum of printmaking and photography in Center City, founded in 1915. It shows changing exhibitions and runs a yearly competition for artists, and paid memberships bring member events and shop discounts.
records.what_you_do: Visit the free galleries during open hours, or join one of its exhibition tours (listed for Oct 23 and Nov 13, 2026). Artists can enter The ANNUAL competition. Individual members and up get invitations to members-only events.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11 am to 6 pm, with free admission. Exhibition tours are listed for Friday Oct 23, 2026 and Friday Nov 13, 2026, both 5:30 to 6 pm. A tour on Wednesday Oct 7, 2026 at noon has already passed.

cost.text: Admission to exhibitions and education programs is free. Membership is optional and costs $30 (student) to $500 (benefactor) a year. The tour cost is not listed.

first_step.how: Come during open hours, or join the Oct 23 exhibition tour. Call the Center at 215.735.6090 first to confirm the tour cost.
first_step.basis: The galleries are free and open to the public with no sign-up. Tours need a listed time.

records.notes: The site says it is undergoing maintenance and some content is unavailable. No classes, workshops or volunteer roles appear on the pages read, so the public roles are visiting, touring, entering the competition and membership. The site does not confirm that tours are free.

records.name: The Resource Exchange
records.summary: A reuse shop and gallery that sells donated and reclaimed art and craft materials at low prices. It runs workshops, a monthly gallery night and volunteer days, and gives artists a gallery call for work made from its materials.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the Oct 24, 2026 volunteer day through the sign-up link, join a workshop such as the Oct 17 block printing session, or visit the shop and the monthly gallery night. Artists can apply to the reCreate gallery call (deadline Nov 10).

schedule.text: The shop and gallery are open Wednesday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and Sunday, noon to 4 pm. Listed events: 2nd Thursday Gallery Night on Oct 8, 5 to 8 pm; a block printing workshop on Oct 17, 11 am to 1 pm; and a volunteer day on Oct 24, 11 am to 2 pm. The event pages give no year, but these weekdays match 2026.

cost.text: The site describes its shop items as affordable; prices are not shown here. Workshop, volunteer and gallery night costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Use the sign-up link on the site to join the Oct 24 volunteer day, or ask about the Oct 17 workshop cost before you come.
first_step.basis: Volunteer days and workshops have listed dates and a sign-up link, and visitors are welcome in the shop and gallery.

records.notes: The batch's IRS address (1114 N 4th St, Apt a) looks like a residence and is not used; the shop address on the group's site is used instead. The newest dated news item is 'Our Impact in 2025', dated Jan 14, 2026. The event pages give no year.

records.name: Theatre Exile
records.summary: A nonprofit theatre in South Philadelphia that stages new and provocative plays. Its education programs include school residencies and camps, and volunteers and ushers can help at the theatre.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as an usher or in the office, which also gives free entry to shows, or join the education programs (school residencies and camps). An open house on Sunday Oct 11, 2026, 3 to 6 pm, is open to visitors, with an RSVP link on the site.

schedule.text: Productions run through its 2026 to 27 season, called Season 30. Usher and volunteer shifts are set per show, and no shift dates are listed. Open house: Sunday Oct 11, 2026, 3 to 6 pm.

cost.text: Single show tickets are sold separately. A 3-show Flex Pass starts at $45. Ushers and volunteers see shows for free.

first_step.how: Fill in the online volunteer and usher form linked from the site, or come to the Oct 11 open house and ask about ushering.
first_step.basis: Usher and volunteer roles are open to the public through a sign-up form. The site lists no training and no minimum age for ushers.

records.notes: The Workshops in Exile page lists only virtual workshops from 2022 and 2023, so no current class is recorded. Its education page describes school residencies and camps with no dates or costs. Its blog posts are dated Sept 2025, and the Oct 11, 2026 open house is the newest dated item on its own site. The internship deadlines on the volunteer page apply to applicants 18 and older; the usher and office roles state no minimum age.

records.name: Tiny Dynamite
records.summary: A Philadelphia theatre company that makes plays at modest ticket prices in a relaxed, social setting. Its shows include pub-style nights with food and drink, and volunteers can usher at shows.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the volunteer form on the site to join the usher list. Ushers see the show for free and get pizza and a drink. You can also buy a ticket to a show or come to a special party.

schedule.text: Show dates are listed on individual event pages. The events page had no dated listings when read, although a 2026 Valentine's Day show and a Jane Austen birthday party appear in the site menu. The 10th anniversary fundraiser has no date.

cost.text: Tickets are at modest prices, but exact prices are not shown on the pages read. Ushers volunteer for free and see the show.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the site to be added to the usher list, then buy a ticket to the next show you want to see.
first_step.basis: The usher form is public and volunteers are contacted when a spot opens. No orientation is described.

records.notes: The events page lists no dated events, only a 10th anniversary fundraiser with no date. The 2026 Valentine's Day show is the newest dated item found, from the site menu. A thank-you message for the 2025/26 season is undated and was read as a recent sign. No public email was found.

records.name: ArtWell Collaborative
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that gives young people a place to make art through writing, music, poetry, visual arts and performance. Most of its work happens in schools and community groups, and its free family days are open to the public.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer in development, design, finance or community engagement by writing to the contact on its Get Involved page, attend a free family day, or come to its poetry and art show. Board members can apply through the board form on the site.

schedule.text: A free family day ran on Sunday Oct 4, 2026, 10 am to 4 pm, held with partner organizations. It is still listed on the site as upcoming. Student programs run in schools and libraries on dates set by each host. The date of the poetry and art show is not listed.

cost.text: The family day is free and volunteering costs nothing. Student program costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Write to the volunteer contact listed on the Get Involved page to offer help, and watch the events page for the next free family day.
first_step.basis: The free family days are open to anyone, and the volunteer roles name a contact to write to.

records.notes: The family day listed for Oct 4, 2026 had already passed by Oct 8 but still appears as upcoming, so check the events page before publishing dates. Student programs are booked by schools and organizations through a request page, so the public way in is the family days, volunteering and the poetry and art show. The newest dated news item is the July 13, 2026 'by the numbers' report. The site names the Barnes Foundation and IPD Philly as partners for the family day; IPD Philly is a lead.

records.name: Philadelphia Asian American Film Foundation
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs a yearly film festival and year-round screenings and talks about Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander stories. Volunteers help run the festival and the year-round work.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer for festival shifts or on a year-round committee (sponsorship, marketing, programming, guest services or volunteer coordination) through the sign-up form on its site. Or attend a fall screening or talk.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 events: a restored 1982 film screening on Sunday Oct 11, 4 to 6 pm; a People's Cinema Club screening on Tuesday Oct 20, 6:30 to 9:30 pm at Village of Industry and Art; and an author talk on Tuesday Oct 20, 7 to 9 pm at the Free Library's Central Library on Vine Street. The 11-day festival runs each year, and its 2026 dates are not listed.

cost.text: Prices for the October events are not listed. Festival volunteers get a shirt and a free ticket to a paid event for each shift. Donations are welcome.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign-up form on the site, or attend the Oct 11 screening and ask about volunteering.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says no film background is needed and gives a sign-up form for newcomers.

records.notes: Festival volunteers help with day-of programming and screenings. The volunteer page does not name ushers; guest services may cover event help, but the page does not say so. The 2026 festival dates are not listed. The Jan 21, 2026 journal posts are the newest dated posts, and the October events are the newest dated listings.

records.name: The Idiopathic Ridculopathy Consortium
records.notes: A real, active theatre company with a 20-year history; the site reports a 2026 anniversary season. Its public roles are buying tickets to productions, a ticketed scavenger hunt fundraiser on Sunday Oct 25, 2026, donations, and a podcast. No class, workshop, volunteer, membership or community program was found, so it is not_a_group under the cultural fund rule. The Sept 27 Instagram reel has no year in the text, so 2026 is inferred from the anniversary season. Re-check if a public program appears. No street address or email is on the site, and the batch PO box is not used.

records.name: The Philadelphia Artists' Collective
records.notes: A professional theatre company. Public roles found: buying tickets or a PAC Pass subscription for its season (The Melting Pot, Oct 21 to Nov 9, 2026), and a three-part free Venture Reading Series with dates still to be announced. No class, workshop, volunteer, membership or community program was found, so it is not_a_group under the cultural fund rule. Re-check when the reading dates are posted or if a class or volunteer role appears. The contact page gives a P.O. box, and the batch IRS address is not used.

records.name: White Box Theatre
records.notes: A theatre company whose current site shows one production, Kea and the Ark, described as suitable for all ages, plus archived work made for other organizations. No current class, workshop, open audition, volunteer or membership role was found. The education page covers only 2010 to 2016 programs and says more recent documentation is to come. The site has no dates. Not_a_group under the cultural fund rule; re-check if current education programs are posted.

records.name: Wear Yellow Proudly
records.notes: A registered 501(c)(3) that presents music by and about Asian Americans. The homepage lists a season, artists, projects, booking and a donation form, but no class, workshop, volunteer, membership or community program. The projects pages returned 404 or gave no detail. Not_a_group under the cultural fund rule for now; re-check the projects pages if they load. The address on the site is an apartment unit, so it is not recorded here.
